title: Minimum Number of Coins for Fruits
summary: Given an array prices where prices[i] represents the coin cost to buy the (i + 1)th fruit, you can get any of the next i fruits for free when purchasing the (i + 1)th fruit.
statement: Given an array prices where prices[i] represents the coin cost to buy the (i + 1)th fruit, you can get any of the next i fruits for free when purchasing the (i + 1)th fruit. You can still buy any fruit for its listed price to get its reward. Find the minimum coins needed to buy all fruits.
constraints: prices is nonempty and prices[i] is the cost of fruit i+1.
Buying fruit i grants any of the next i fruits for free, but a free-eligible fruit may still be bought for its reward.
Return the minimum coins needed to acquire every fruit.
hints: The next paid fruit determines all future choices; free eligibility does not forbid buying it.
Memoize the minimum cost when fruit position is the next required purchase.
Pay its price and choose the next purchase among positions position+1 through 2*position+1; stop when coverage reaches the end.
Every valid strategy has one next paid fruit in exactly that range, and the recurrence enumerates all such choices while memoization preserves the cheapest suffix.
editorial: Every valid strategy has one next paid fruit in exactly that range, and the recurrence enumerates all such choices while memoization preserves the cheapest suffix.

tests.explanation: Buy fruits one and two for four coins; fruit three is then free.
Buy fruits one and three for two coins, covering the other fruits as rewards.
